I'll start by reading the release plan and discovering the deploy tools.

The plan has 12 services to process. I'll list the services, then build all 12 commits in parallel.

Staging is done for five services. `orders-api` already has b-45 live and healthy in both environments, so it needs no deploys. `notify-worker` and `catalog-svc` still need staging deploys.

Now I'll check the health of the newly deployed staging releases.

The `email-worker` rollback hit a connection reset, so I can't tell whether it took effect. I'll check its staging status before retrying anything.

The rollback did take effect: staging is back on b-30 as release r-85, so I won't repeat it. Now I'll write the report and status files.

I worked through all 12 services with `hold` set to `no`, and left `edge-gateway` and `ledger-api` alone because they're held. I wrote `/app/release-report.json` and `/app/STATUS.json` (status `success`).

- **Promoted (7):** `auth-api`, `billing-api`, `catalog-svc`, `checkout-web`, `inventory-sync`, `notify-worker` and `orders-api`.
  - `auth-api` was already live and healthy in staging, so I only deployed it to prod.
  - `orders-api` already had the build live in both environments, so I made no deploys.
- **Failed build (2):** `cart-svc` and `search-api`. I didn't deploy either.
- **Degraded (3):** `email-worker`, `pricing-svc` and `session-svc`.
  - I deployed `email-worker` and `pricing-svc` to staging, found them degraded, and rolled each back once.
  - `session-svc` was already live and degraded in staging when I checked, so I left staging as it was.

Some calls failed along the way:
- **`email-worker` rollback:** It returned a connection reset, so I checked its status before retrying. The rollback had taken effect (staging is on b-30 as r-85), so I didn't repeat it.
- **Build calls:** Two returned empty or truncated output. I re-ran them, and both came back as cached builds, so no duplicate builds were created.
- **Rate limit:** One status call hit a rate limit and I re-ran it. None of these failures led to a repeated deploy or rollback.
